chunks: 1929 - And ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī narrated from Sahl ibn Saʿd, who said:

I heard al-Riḍā عليه السلام saying: “Fasting is upon sighting, and breaking the fast is upon sighting; and he is not from us who fasts before the sighting for the sighting, and breaks the fast before the sighting for the sighting.”
He said: I said to him, “O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, what do you hold regarding the fasting of the day of doubt?”

So he said: “My father narrated to me from my grandfather, from his forefathers عليهم السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: ‘That I fast one day from the month of Shaʿbān is more beloved to me than that I break the fast one day from the month of Ramaḍān.’”

key_terms.الرُّؤْيَةِ: the sighting of the crescent that determines the start or end of fasting
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: sawm; fasting as the religious observance being discussed
key_terms.الْفِطْرُ: breaking the fast, here meaning ending Ramaḍān upon valid sighting
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, the obligatory month of sawm
key_terms.شَهْرِ شَعْبَانَ: the month of Shaʿbān, the month preceding Ramaḍān
key_terms.يَوْمِ الشَّكِّ: the day of doubt, when it is uncertain whether Ramaḍān has begun

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about moon sighting and fasting on the day of doubt?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the beginning and ending of the fast are determined by the sighting of the crescent. It also addresses the day of doubt, indicating the caution of fasting it as a day of Shaʿbān rather than risking omission of a day from Ramaḍān. The report reflects the guidance of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام on proper observance of sawm.
